name: Purchase to pay (SAP Ariba with SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud)
system: SAP Ariba Buying and Invoicing with SAP S/4HANA Cloud, public edition
note: Written by the Glasstarn project from public knowledge of SAP Ariba reporting and SAP's released S/4HANA Cloud data views. Requisitions, approvals and supplier invoices received in Ariba come from Ariba report exports; orders, goods movements, invoices and payments from the S/4HANA Cloud views, linked by the ERP order and invoice numbers Ariba keeps. Not yet confirmed on a real Ariba site or tenant; tested only on made-up files.

size_check.ask: How many purchase order items were created in the period for the company code?

checks.label: Ariba requisitions whose SAP order is in the export

question.text: {missing} of {total} Ariba requisitions ({missing_share}) point to SAP orders that are not in the SAP export, usually orders created after the period or in another company code. They stay in the analysis as requisitions without an order. Is that fine?

options.label: Fine, keep them as they are
Ask the SAP admin to export those orders too

question.text: {missing} of {total} Ariba orders ({missing_share}) have no matching order in the SAP export. Either the SAP export misses them (another company code or period) or they failed to reach SAP. Which is it?

options.label: The SAP export misses them; export them too
They did not reach SAP; treat that as a finding

checks.label: SAP orders that came through Ariba

question.text: {missing} of {total} SAP orders ({missing_share}) were created directly in SAP, not through Ariba. Is that allowed for some purchases, or is it buying outside the agreed process?

options.label: Not allowed; treat it as a finding

checks.label: approved Ariba invoices found in SAP

question.text: {missing} of {total} invoices approved in Ariba ({missing_share}) have no matching invoice in the SAP export. Either the SAP export misses them (another period or company code) or they did not reach SAP. Which is it?

options.label: The SAP export misses them; export them too
They did not reach SAP; treat that as a finding
